• Premium (ToF/LiDAR) — Hardware depth sensors deliver ±2cm accuracy. Ideal for construction and precise work.

• High (Depth API) — Software depth estimation with ±5cm precision. Available on most modern devices.

• Standard (ARCore) — Surface detection and feature tracking with ±10cm accuracy.

• Basic (Camera) — Camera-based estimation for devices without AR support.

1. Tap the Measure button or select a tool

2. Point your camera at the target

3. Wait for the green indicator (optimal conditions)

4. Align the crosshair and tap to measure

• Tracking status — Is ARCore actively tracking?

Turn your phone into a heart rate monitor. Place a fingertip on the rear camera and see your pulse in about 15 seconds. No smartwatch, no account, no internet connection needed.

[How the Measurement Works]

Your fingertip becomes the sensor. The flash shines into your finger, and blood absorbs far more of that light than the skin and tissue around it. Every heartbeat pushes a fresh pulse of blood into your fingertip, so the camera image darkens very slightly with each beat and brightens again as the pulse passes. The app reads the average brightness of about 30 frames every second, and the rise and fall of those values traces your pulse wave. How often that wave repeats is your BPM. This optical method is called photoplethysmography (PPG), the same principle behind the sensor lights on the back of a smartwatch. Every reading comes with a confidence score, so you always know how much to trust the number.
